author: Zintenka
body:
I made a suggestion to this in the Rules Rules Rules thread. Mooch suggested that i make a separate topic about this. Many other kill farm topics went horridly with the problem not being resolved or enforced.

Make it illegal to kill-farm; please. If new players come and play and their first experience wasnt good then they will leave.

You may say that it is a tactic, yes it is. A very dirty one. And we all know that players that kill farm dont do it for "tactics". They do it to gloat and stroke their own pride saying "eZ" or "Wow the enemy team sucks."

This "tactic" shows no sportsmanship for your opponent and shows that you use dishonorable means to gain the upper hand.

Remember when spawn blocking was considered a "tactic"? This is the same. Please enforce this rule and you will have funner games for everyone. I know that you guys know that I'm right.

And to those of you who say that it is sportful then just look at the act's name. "Kill-farm". That means you are referring the enemy to cattle or fodder and not your fellow man. This in itself is very disrespectful and cocky. 

Many ppl who agree that kill farming should stay legal are donors. 90% of them. 

Dont you agree that this is suspicious? Its not a coincidence either. 

The team that is kill farming usually has a lot of donators and donors who are regulars. And they also have moderators on them as well. Very suspicious. 

Then the team who is being kill farmed will have donors who leave and stack the other team; making it even worse.

"It makes me very appalled that moderators would allow and support this. We want a better and funner network with new players who want to stay. 

We help by making a very good impression of ourselves. This, among other things should be rectified. I just feel that this is one of the highest concerns to me."

- Zintenka, 2014

Here is MY opinion of what Quintus should look like: 

  • If you are passing through the red zone to get to their monuments then by all means pass on through. If enemies are in your way, kill them.

But if you plan on staying there and not going after objectives and "farm" enemies like cattle then that should be a verbal warn, then a kick if you do not heed the warning. Second time offenders should be temp-banned. 

My reasons for drawing:
  • The team should have access to their own iron supply to fend off invaders. 
  • The team that is being attacked showed not be killed as soon as they leave spawn.
Any objections?

replies.body: I personally like kill farming, but here's what I have to say. Sure, kill farming is annoying to new players and such, but it's hard to avoid. Even though it's bad for non-donors and new players, they always have the option to leave. My favorite maps to kill farm on are the Justice trio. On these maps, I don't go very close to the spawn, I just hold a choke point. This way, the enemies are able to go to their iron supply freely and have a chance at killing me. If I'm up closer to their spawn, I don't attack unless they attack me first. If they want to run past me and avoid me, fine. Maps like Quintus don't really need to have more rules tacked on however. I've attempted to play on the "kill farmed team" and it's only bad when the kill farming team is shooting into spawn or camping the walkway to the iron deposits. The thing about the iron supply camping however, should be allowed. The people that get killed there are choosing to go over there, and most maps have a 2nd/3rd iron deposit where they can get armor. Just my two cents.

replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
Kill farmers have no tactical intentions and only mean to brag and boast pretentiously? And this is something “we all” know? Hopefully that categorical generalization doesn’t include me, because I know someone who does not accord with your claims and maintains a good sportsmanship — myself.

As a regular player who often farms kills on most maps (Abandoned Park II, Teres, Senex II, and Rendezvous III, to name a few), I don’t charge at the opposing team only wishing to raise my K/D or to belittle others; honestly, I do it to divert the attention of as many people as possible, for as long as I’m able, and to gain a lot of experience points (admittedly a bit selfish). Regardless of whatever original purpose I have, serving as a distraction tends to double up as an additional function.

Why do people view kill farming as so dishonorable and wretched? Unless you create a choke point that directly impedes the enemy’s movements to and from their spawn area and armor supply — I personally have never done that — only credulous people will fall for your trap, and that’s their fault.

Personally, my method of kill farming is passive; I only attack people that come to me. For instance, on Senex II, I hide in the far corners of the gold piles. If people want to keep coming back to me, that’s by their own will. If they want to craft armor first, from the same gold stash, they’re free to do so.

On the other hand, on maps such as Unix, I occasionally find myself trapped on the opposite side of the map, usually in the enchanting room. Though I may have originally wandered in with the hopes of surprising a pack of five unsuspecting players, that may quickly turn into myself getting swarmed by hordes of enemies, fighting for my survival, unable to backtrack back to my own team’s defenses. Would that still be considered kill farming?

Quintus, among others, is a completely different story — it’s very common to see people stationed directly in front of the opponent’s spawn. I wholly support your suggestion for kill farms to not be allowed beyond the color demarcation, as that would be preventing the other team from crafting armor and even leaving the spawn dome through its main exit. However, I don’t think a total statute against all forms of kill farming would be fair for those who aren’t as belligerent.

Spawn blocking is on a separate paradigm. It blatantly hinders the affected team’s maneuverability by limiting something as simplistic as their ways of leaving their spawn. Passive kill farming, as I mentioned earlier, isn’t an active interference. For that reason, I believe it should have a higher leniency.

Using the name of the tactic as support for your argument isn’t very convincing, though I do see your logic and it makes sense. Still, there are many ways to describe one thing. Servant, or slave? An accident, or manslaughter? Unhappy, or inconsolable? Kill farming, or a dangerous diversion? It’s dependent on how you look at it. Perhaps “kill farm” was the most comprehensible and succinct name, though this is a debatable topic.

Count me as one of the non-donors who advocates the continued permitting of kill farming, please.

replies.author: Zieno12345
replies.body:
Kill farmers have no tactical intentions and only mean to brag and boast pretentiously? Actually yes, many players kill farm for their K/D, though there are a few exceptions (e.g. you)

I do it to divert the attention of as many people as possible, for as long as I’m able, and to gain a lot of experience points (admittedly a bit selfish). Regardless of whatever original purpose I have, serving as a distraction tends to double up as an additional function. Though there is a tactical function, the process is the same. Additionally, the kill farming team usually breaks the monuments in the end, so both processes are essentially indifferent 

Why do people view kill farming as so dishonorable and wretched? Kill farming is seen negatively because it thwarts a team's abilities to break the objective. The team instead must fend off players that are killing them repeatedly which isn't fun and is usually unsuccessful. 

Personally, my method of kill farming is passive; I only attack people that come to me. Considering the fact that you're stationed on the opposing team's side, it is completely understandable why this (see below) scenario would happen. Players are naturally inclined to kill players they consider a threat--this status gained by simply crossing to their side.

Though I may have originally wandered in with the hopes of surprising a pack of five unsuspecting players, that may quickly turn into myself getting swarmed by hordes of enemies, fighting for my survival, unable to backtrack back to my own team’s defenses. Would that still be considered kill farming? 

Kill farming, or a dangerous diversion? It’s dependent on how you look at it. Perhaps “kill farm” was the most comprehensible and succinct name, though this is a debatable topic. Though the connotation of the words "kill farming" is seen negatively, "dangerous diversion" indirectly provides the same outcome: killing the opposing team repeatedly.

Would that still be considered kill farming? 

Kill farming, or a dangerous diversion? It’s dependent on how you look at it. Perhaps “kill farm” was the most comprehensible and succinct name, though this is a debatable topic. Though the connotation of the words "kill farming" is seen negatively, "dangerous diversion" indirectly provides the same outcome: killing the opposing team repeatedly.

Though all the points made here are true, I still disagree with this. I don't killfarm a lot, but when I do, I never say "ez" after it, because as Emmy said, that's rude. There are plenty of ways to get iron while the other team is camping it, if you do it correctly. You can sneak along the bottom edge of the map, using wood, and digging more than enough blocks, for your entire team, all without getting caught.

Also, while a killfarm is going on, it is extremely easy to win the game, if all the players are killfarming. Tactics include wallsprinting so they can't catch up to you, since they won't chase you on a wall with diamond armor. Another tactic is to skybridge if they covered the walkway completely, or get water from a monument and bridge under bedrock.
